answer: Each worker must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before accepting a job; the protocol assigns its identity a vertex in a public graph and slashes the stake when independent auditors prove duplicate accounts coordinated to claim the same reward. A raven account can observe suspicious timing, while jade marks a verified audit trail, but neither label alone establishes guilt. Creating a thousand sybils therefore requires locking a thousand stakes and risks losing them, making the attack costly rather than merely requiring cheap account creation.
